The app can now be set to Spanish, English, Italian or Russian from the Language menu, without changing your phone\'s language.
The morning report and the widget speak the language you picked too, and the report now arrives with the icon of the weather ahead.
The data cards look cleaner: the background fades out and there is no longer a box drawn around each value.
The big card in the grid now starts next to the others instead of floating on its own, and the sun on the Sun and moon arc animates when the card reaches the middle of the screen.

Every data card now has its own animated icon: precipitation, chance of rain, UV index, solar radiation, dew point, pressure, elevation, pollen, historical comparison, swell, rivers, climate change, uncertainty, sunrise, sunset, moon phase and daylight hours.
The week now shows as a carousel: each day is a card that rotates and faces forward as it passes the center.
Each day of the week has its own photo, chosen based on that day\'s weather, and changes daily.
The carousel can be dragged from anywhere on the screen and keeps spinning when you let go, instead of stopping abruptly.
Rotating your phone shows the whole week at a glance: the center card large and the rest shrinking toward the sides.
The icons in the top corner are now grouped into a side menu, each section with its name shown.
On \"Today\", the city name stays fixed at the top and shrinks as you scroll down, making room for the content.
The \"Today\" cards sweep in as they appear on screen.
Photo credits now update themselves: authors of the photos currently in use appear, and ones no longer shown disappear.
Each credit is now a link: it leads to the author\'s profile and to the original photo on Unsplash.
The hourly chart now starts by showing rain, and its background changes color throughout the hours: coral at dawn, golden during the day, green in the afternoon and blue at night.
Data cards are now arranged in three columns and animate in: a large card shrinks into place while the rest appear around it.
The sun and moon card now sits at the very top and, when it reaches the center of the screen, the sun or moon travels along its arc before settling at the current time.
New \"Sun and moon\" card showing the sun\'s path, daylight hours and the current moon phase.
The background changes depending on whether it\'s morning, afternoon or night.
The widget can now be shown with a photo, transparent, or with a solid color of your choice.
Additional data now loads much faster.
Smoother scroll animation on the Today screen.
Photo author credits on the Info screen.
First version: today\'s forecast and the next 7 days.
Hourly chart for temperature, rain and wind.
Configurable additional data: UV, pollen, swell, rivers, historical comparison and more.
Morning report: a daily notification at the time you choose.
There\'s no blog yet. You\'ll soon find articles here about the weather and the app\'s updates.
Weather forecast app. Data from Open-Meteo, backgrounds from Unsplash.
Tempovole is offered \"as is\", for informational purposes, with no guarantee of availability or accuracy of the data shown.

Weather data comes from Open-Meteo and may contain errors or delays; don\'t use this app as the sole source for decisions affecting your safety (for example, alerts for severe weather events) — always check official sources for that.
Use that damages, overloads or compromises the app or the third-party services it depends on (Open-Meteo, Unsplash) is not permitted.
These terms may be updated; continued use of the app after a change implies acceptance of it.
Tempovole doesn\'t require registration or an account, and doesn\'t collect personally identifiable data.

Location: the app doesn\'t use the device\'s GPS. By default it shows Barcelona; if you search for another city in Settings, the text you type is sent to Open-Meteo\'s geocoder to obtain its coordinates, which are stored only on your device.

Weather data: to show the forecast and the additional data you enable in Settings (air quality and pollen, historical comparison, swell, rivers, climate change, model uncertainty), the coordinates of the chosen location are sent to Open-Meteo\'s various free services. No other data is sent.

Photos: if an Unsplash key is configured, the app requests from Unsplash (api.unsplash.com) the background photo for each part of the day and the photos for the week\'s cards, and notifies it which photos are used, as its guidelines require. Only the search term (for example \"rain\") is sent, never personal data.
Daily notification and widget: these are generated on the device itself and query the same Open-Meteo services (and Unsplash, for the widget background) described above to show up-to-date weather.
The app doesn\'t use accounts, cookies, advertising identifiers or analytics or tracking tools, and doesn\'t share data with third parties beyond the calls to Open-Meteo and Unsplash described above.
All settings (location, notification time, enabled data, etc.) are stored only on the device and are deleted when the app is uninstalled.
View this policy in your browser

Photos come from Unsplash and are used under its license. Each photo is the work of its author: the app shows one as a background in the morning, afternoon and night, and another on each of the week\'s cards based on that day\'s weather. Below are the authors of the photos the app is currently using; tap any of them to see their profile.
No photo has been shown yet: its author will appear here as soon as the first one loads.
The weather icons (animated and static) come from Flaticon and are used under its free license, which requires attribution.
The highest temperature forecast for today, typically reached in the early afternoon. It helps you decide how to dress and whether to avoid the hottest hours.
The lowest temperature forecast for today, usually in the early morning or at sunrise. Useful to know if you\'ll need a coat when heading out early.
Maximum wind speed forecast for today, measured at 10 meters above ground. From 40-50 km/h it can make walking or holding an umbrella difficult; above 60 km/h are considered strong gusts.

Total amount of rain (or other precipitation) forecast for the whole day, in millimeters. 1 mm equals 1 liter of water per square meter: less than 1 mm is barely noticeable, over 10 mm is already significant rain.
Probability of rain at some point during the day, according to the weather model. Above 50%% it\'s worth carrying an umbrella; below 20%% rain is unlikely.

Measures the intensity of the sun\'s ultraviolet radiation, on a scale from 0 to 11+. An index of 6 or higher calls for sun protection; from 8 upward you should avoid direct sun during the middle of the day.
Solar energy reaching the surface right now, in watts per square meter (W/m²). Values above 700-800 W/m² indicate very strong sun, typical of a clear summer midday.
The temperature at which air becomes saturated with moisture and starts to condense. Below 10° it feels dry; above 20° the air feels muggy, even if the air temperature itself isn\'t very high.
Air pressure at surface level, in hectopascals (hPa). Around 1013 hPa is average pressure; lower values are usually associated with bad weather, and higher ones with stable, clear weather.
Height above sea level of the chosen location. It affects temperature (higher elevation, cooler air) and solar radiation, which is more intense the higher up you go.
Concentration of the predominant pollen type in the air right now, measured in grains per cubic meter. Only available in Europe. High levels can affect people with seasonal allergies.

Difference between today\'s average temperature and the historical average for this same day over the last 15 years. A positive value means it\'s warmer than usual for this date; a negative one, that it\'s colder.
Wave height in the nearest sea to this location, in meters. Data is only available if the location is on the coast or very close to the sea. Above 2 meters is already considered rough sea.

Estimated discharge of the nearest river according to a global hydrological model, in cubic meters per second. Only available near rivers covered by the model; it\'s a reference, not an official flood alert.
Difference between the projected average annual temperature for 2050 (according to a climate model) and that of a recent real year. Gives an idea of how much this area could warm up in the long term.
Temperature range for the current hour according to the different simulations (members) of the ensemble weather model. The wider the range, the less certain the model is about the exact outcome.
Average of all the day\'s temperatures. It\'s a more representative picture of \"how the day felt\" overall than looking only at the high or the low.
The time the sun rises today at this location. It changes throughout the year depending on the season and the location\'s latitude.
The time the sun sets today at this location, marking the end of natural daylight hours.

The moon goes through 8 phases over a cycle of about 29.5 days, alternating between new moon (almost invisible) and full moon (fully visible). Useful to know if there\'ll be a bit more light at night.
Total time between today\'s sunrise and sunset. It varies throughout the year depending on the season and latitude: days are longer in summer and shorter in winter.
Shown in \"Today\": sunrise and sunset time, daylight hours and the current moon phase.
Atmospheric data (UV, radiation, dew point, pressure)
Shown in \"Today\": UV index, solar radiation, dew point and atmospheric pressure.
Shows the predominant pollen type and its level. Data is only available in Europe.
Adds the elevation above sea level of the chosen location.
Compares today\'s temperature with the average of the last 15 years on this date.
Wave height of the nearest sea. Data is only available if you\'re on the coast.
Estimated discharge of the nearest river, if one is covered by the model.
Difference between the projected average temperature for 2050 and a recent year.
Temperature range according to the different simulations of the weather model.
Uses the same background photo as the app, based on the time of day.
No background: your phone\'s wallpaper shows through the widget.
A solid color of your choice.
